dish: Awanami (泡波) — Hateruma's 'phantom' awamori from island sugarcane
n: Hateruma Shuzōsho — Awanami distillery, Hateruma Island (波照間酒造所)
address: Hateruma Island, Taketomi, Yaeyama, Okinawa, Japan
w: The only distillery on Hateruma, Japan's southernmost inhabited island, making Awanami — the so-called 'phantom awamori' that sells out within minutes; bottles and Awanami goods are sold at the distillery shop.

dish: Yonaguni hanazake (花酒) — 60-proof first-run spirit; awamori 'Yonaguni' and 'Kuba-maki'
n: Sakimoto Shuzōsho — hanazake distillery, Yonaguni (崎元酒造所)
w: Yonaguni's oldest distillery, still firing a traditional direct-fire pot still by hand; maker of the awamori 'Yonaguni' and of hanazake, the 60% first-run spirit that only Yonaguni is permitted to make. Distillery shop sells brewery-only bottles.

dish: Ishigaki-jima rāyu (the original 'edible chilli oil') and jājan-suba noodles
address: Ishigaki city centre (7 min walk from Ishigaki bus terminal), Ishigaki, Okinawa, Japan
w: Birthplace of Ishigaki-jima rāyu, the hand-made island-salt-and-chilli oil that started Japan's 'edible rāyu' boom; at lunch the house order is jājan-suba (thick noodles with spicy miso), served until sold out.

address: 360 Ihara, Ishigaki, Okinawa, Japan (Akashi area, north Ishigaki)
w: Old-guard north-Ishigaki shokudō about 40 minutes' drive from town, with queues before opening for its soft-bone sōki Yaeyama soba — clean pork-bone broth over round straight noodles. Ranked No.1 in a 2019 Okinawa-soba ranking reported by Ryukyu Shimpo.

dish: Ganso gyū-jiru soba (original Ishigaki-beef broth soba)
n: Arakaki Shokudō, Ishigaki — CLOSED (新垣食堂)
w: Ihara shokudō whose beef-broth soba, made with beef from the family's own ranch, won the original-soup division of the first Yaeyama Soba Championship. CLOSED: it shut on 27 November after 35 years (Yaeyama Mainichi).

n: Kuninaka Shokudō, Miyako (くになか食堂)
w: Locals' Miyako-soba shokudō in Miyakojima city, picked in Rurubu's eight best Miyako soba and in Mapple's Miyako dining list.
